Chris Gober

Republican candidate for U.S. Representative, District 10, Travis County, Texas · Open seat

Attorney (Republican election and campaign-finance lawyer)

Chris Gober is a Republican attorney who served in 2024 as director and chief lawyer of America PAC, the super PAC founded by Elon Musk. He is running for the open seat in Texas' 10th Congressional District, which Rep. Michael McCaul is leaving. He won the 10-candidate Republican primary on March 3, 2026 with about 51% of the vote, avoiding a runoff, and faces Democrat Caitlin Rourk on November 3, 2026.

Where Gober stands

Federal agencies and government overreach
Says federal agencies have been used to intimidate, censor and silence conservatives, and pledges to oppose what he calls bureaucratic overreach that threatens freedoms.
Free speech and elections
Says he has spent his legal career defending free speech, election integrity and the Constitution in court, and will continue these priorities in Congress.
Economy and rural communities
Pledges to support policies that grow Texas's economy while protecting rural communities. Says the district's interests range from the Austin tech corridor to farming and ranching.
Border security
Lists securing the border among his reasons for running for Congress.
Relationship with President Trump
Says he is running to stand with President Trump and describes himself as an America First conservative endorsed by Trump.

Background

  • Republican nominee, U.S. House Texas District 10 (won March 3, 2026 primary with about 51%)
  • Director and chief lawyer, America PAC (2024)
  • Attorney; involved in Texas's 2025 mid-decade congressional redistricting (per news reports)
  • Education: Texas A&M University; Harvard Law School (J.D.)
  • Has held no elected office
